conviction_note: Two forces on this print. The reported quarter should land slightly above a consensus that sits inside the company's guide, and this name has bought its last two beats (+5.0%, +11.5%). Against that, the FY guide arithmetic needs Q4 to accelerate, and the same Q3 print a year ago cut the outlook (-20.8%). Over the whole print hangs an unresolved GTCR sale process that the stock has been de-rating for five days. The findings sum to -1.2 and the scaled number is -0.5 (p_up 48 x abs 12). The scaled number is smaller because the sale-process binary is roughly symmetric in direction and goes into abs_move_pct, not the sign.

findings.finding: SPS has a live sale process. Reuters reported in June that Morgan Stanley was hired after pressure from activists Irenic and Anson. Bloomberg reported on 2026-09-11 that GTCR was in talks, with a deal 'could be announced in the coming weeks'; the stock jumped up to 16% intraday and closed +7.1%. Seven weeks later there is no 8-K, no 13D change, and no Form 4 filed by any insider since 2026-06-01 (EDGAR submissions; the latest filing is a 2026-08-14 13G). The company announced on 2026-10-15 an ordinary Q3 release with a conference call, and the stock has given back 7.8% in five sessions. The print is the first time management must speak publicly since the GTCR report. Outcomes are (a) a deal announced with results, a large positive; (b) 'review concluded' or analysts concluding talks are dead, a large negative toward the pre-rumor ~$78; (c) 'no comment', which leaves fundamentals in charge. Two facts weigh on the odds. A normal call being scheduled leans mildly against a signed deal tonight. Insider Form 4 silence since June is consistent with a blackout while talks are live.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior earnings print inside a sale process. The only reaction to sale news is 2026-09-11: up to +15.8% intraday, close +7.1% on the Bloomberg GTCR report (Motley Fool, Bloomberg Law). Peer DSGX rose 7.4% the same day.
findings.why_not_priced: The deal odds are partly priced. The stock carries a premium of roughly 8% over the 2026-09-09 close of $78.26 (Motley Fool quote page), and the last five sessions show the market fading it. What is not priced is the resolution. If the market were sure of a deal, SPSC would trade near a takeout price above $90, not 19% below its 52-week high and sliding. If it were sure talks had died, the premium over $78 would be gone. The implied move of 11.6% is about the name's own median reaction (11.5%), so options are not paying extra for a deal binary on top of the usual print risk.
findings.independence: Documents: the GTCR report (Bloomberg Law 2026-09-11; Motley Fool https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/09/11/why-sps-commerce-rallied-on-friday/); the call announcement (https://finviz.com/news/403297/sps-commerce-announces-date-of-third-quarter-2026-financial-results, 2026-10-15); and EDGAR submissions (https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001092699.json), which show no Form 4 since 2026-06-01 and no 8-K since 2026-07-30. The deal-odds read rests on all three together, and the Form 4 silence is an inference.

findings.finding: Arithmetic from the company's own FY2026 guide puts the risk on Q4. FY $788.4-793.4M less Q1 $192.1M, Q2 $197.8M and the Q3 guide midpoint $197.3M implies Q4 revenue of $201.2-206.2M (midpoint $203.7M). That is +5.7% reported against Q4 2025's $192.7M, despite about $5.25M of quarterly revenue lost to the 3P Revenue Recovery divestiture. Ex-divestiture, the implied Q4 grows about 8.4% against about 6.7% for the Q3 guide. That is sequential growth of +3.2%, against +1.5% in Q4 2025 (192.7 vs 189.9). The ramp rests on enablement programs 'expected to contribute in the second half'. A secondary call summary says Q2 1P customers fell by over 200 'due to timing of enablement programs'. If Q3 beats by $1-2M, the implied ramp eases. If it does not, the Q4 guide or the FY range is at risk on the same Q3 print that cut the FY outlook a year ago.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance is the line this stock trades on. 2025-10-30 (the same Q3 print a year ago): FY outlook cut, -20.84%. 2025-07-30: -21.99% on guidance. 2026-02-12: -4.37% on a 6-7% 2026 guide with a slight Q4 revenue miss. 2026-07-30: +11.48% when Q2 beat the top of the guide and FY was held ex-divestiture.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus is pinned to the guide: revenue $197.51M, estimates flat for 60 days (Investing.com 10-29). Previews discuss the Q3 number and the divestiture headwind, not the Q4 acceleration the FY range requires. If the market priced a Q4 cut, the stock would not be holding a premium over its 50-day and 200-day averages, and analysts would not have been raising targets into the print (Stifel $70 to $85 on 10-14). Q3 2025 ($189.9M) and Q4 2025 ($192.7M) come from the Q4 2025 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1092699/000109269926000007/er_q425.htm, FY2025 revenue $751.5M).
findings.independence: This uses a second primary document, the Q4 2025 8-K, for the comparison base. The 1P-customer decline comes from a secondary call summary (https://stocktaper.com/earningsCallSummary/SPSC/2026/Q2, snippet_only; the page returned HTTP 429). The finding shares the Q2 8-K with the reported-quarter finding but reads a different line of it, the FY range, not the quarter.

findings.finding: SPS beat the top of its own guide last quarter. Q2 revenue was $197.8M against a guide of $194.5-196.5M, 0.7% above the top. Non-GAAP EPS was $1.27 against $1.06-1.09, and adjusted EBITDA was $66.6M against $60.9-62.4M. Repurchases were $51.2M in the quarter ($98.4M in H1), shrinking the share count to 36.0M. Q1 revenue of $192.1M also grew 6%. On that pattern, Q3 revenue of about $199M and EPS of about $1.28-1.30 against consensus of $197.5M and $1.23 is the base case, a beat of about 0.8% on revenue.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last two beats were bought: 2026-04-30 +4.99% and 2026-07-30 +11.48% on Q2 beating the top of the guide. Earlier beats in 2025 were sold or swamped by the guide: 2025-04-24 -0.88%, 2025-02-10 -13.8%.
findings.why_not_priced: Most of it is priced. A small beat against a guide-pinned consensus is the street's default. If the market expected a large beat, consensus EPS would sit above the $1.23 top of the guide rather than at it. What is left is the size of the EPS overshoot: Q2 cleared the top of the guide by $0.18.
findings.independence: The Q1 2026 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001092699/000109269926000042/er_q126.htm) shows the same guide-then-beat cadence on EBITDA and EPS. This finding shares the Q2 8-K with the guidance finding.

findings.finding: Peer Descartes Systems reported record revenue of $201.1M for its quarter ended 2026-07-31, up 12% year over year, with services up 13%, adjusted EBITDA up 18% and a 47% margin. That points to steady logistics and supply-chain software demand through July, which overlaps one month of SPS's Q3 (July-September).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no measured SPSC reaction to Descartes prints. DSGX moved +7.4% with SPSC on the 2026-09-11 deal report, so the two trade together.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a public, seven-week-old proxy with partial overlap of the quarter and is largely in the price. It is filed small because it is the only counterparty or peer read that spoke after SPS's July call.
findings.independence: This is a proxy, not confirmed by SPS or a direct customer. Descartes's growth includes acquisitions, so organic transmission to SPS's EDI network is unconfirmed.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. A 5-day -7.8% into the print against a flat 20-day says the market is already removing deal premium, and the mild negative lean here goes the same way, so most of the negative may be priced. Moderate short interest (7.9%, 5.7 days) and a possible deal announcement are the upside tail.
lessons_applied: Rules 1 and 6: the reported-quarter beat lands mostly inside a guide-pinned consensus, so it was cut from +0.8 to +0.6. The name's last two beats were bought, so it was not cut to zero.
Rule 3: the two sale-process facts (call scheduled vs Form 4 silence) were already merged into one finding with one sign. Unchanged at -0.5.
Rule 7: short interest was checked before the negatives (7.9%, 5.68 DTC, not crowded) and the baseline has no skew. The Q4 guidance negative is unchanged.
Rule 5: Descartes stays a small proxy at +0.2. abs_move_pct and p_up are unchanged.
